clue.text: He's responsible for the water supply — off and on

definitions.text: He's responsible for the water supply — off and on

parts.words: He's responsible for the water supply — off and on
parts.note: describes the official who works the street valves of a water main, turning the flow off and on again

explanation.walkthrough: 'off and on' looks like 'intermittently', but it is literal: this water-board worker's job was turning the supply off and on at the stopcock.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-company official who opens and shuts the mains valves controls the supply to the street.

clue.text: One river in ten will contain food for the table

definitions.text: will contain food for the table

indicators.note: the river is placed in the number word

parts.note: taken as written
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river among ten will hold the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, which flows into the Ouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep lidded dish is used to serve soup at the dining table.

clue.text: Concerned with an engineer on a ship getting a break

parts.note: RE means regarding or concerning
CE is civil engineer
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A ship's engineer gets some time off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the engineer above the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or interval in work, as Parliament takes between sittings.

clue.text: Not in favour of a brochure constituting an agreement

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: Opposing a pamphlet that sets out a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A binding deal between parties is a legal agreement.

clue.text: Arouse just about everyone

parts.note: C (circa) means about or approximately
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Wake nearly every person.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone in the morning is to wake them.

clue.text: The lad may be brought to a standstill

indicators.note: the letters of the two words may be turned into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A boy might be stopped in his tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' asks for the letters of THE LAD to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopped is the plain synonym: something brought to a standstill has been stopped.

clue.text: Tell say, being more wily

definitions.meaning: William Tell, the Swiss hero who shot an apple from his son's head, is an example of a bowman
arch means cunning or sly, so this is its comparative

explanation.definitionFit: William Tell was a famous bowman; and the comparative of arch, meaning sly, is spelt the same way.

clue.text: The adolescent brew green tea

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and stew ingredients together, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A youngster makes a pot of green tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' looks like a verb for tea, but it rearranges GREEN TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged thirteen to nineteen is a youth or adolescent.

clue.text: Underworld bloomer resulting in bad accident

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A hellish blunder ends in a nasty crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flower, the aster.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe or calamity is a very serious accident.

clue.text: It's not long since bank would accept foreign coin

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
a cent is a coin of the USA and other countries, foreign to a British solver

explanation.surface: A remark that a bank would only lately take overseas money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is the verb here, as in banking on someone, not a financial institution; 'would accept' signals that one piece takes the coin inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately: something that happened lately happened not long ago.

clue.text: Approach for credit?

definitions.meaning: a way in or means of reaching a place
A well-known British credit card, now gone

explanation.definitionFit: Approach as a way in or entry; credit for the old British credit card brand of that name, hence the query.

clue.text: Showing irritation with carrying cash in this country

indicators.note: the outer words carry the cash inside them

parts.note: ire is anger or irritation
and means together with
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross about carrying money around the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republic on the western island of the British Isles is a nation.

clue.text: Guarantee result will be about right

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: to result is to follow as a consequence, to ensue

explanation.surface: A promise that the outcome will be correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' is the verb (ensue), not the noun; 'about' wraps ENSUE round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of something is to guarantee it.

clue.text: Learns as re-writing new magazines

indicators.note: writing the letters out afresh in a new order signals an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone picks up skills by redrafting fresh periodicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-writing new' rearranges the letters of LEARNS AS; 'magazines' means stores of weapons, not periodicals.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is also a store for arms and ammunition, as an armoury is.

clue.text: Clemency — but not for all

definitions.meaning: mercy shown to a beaten enemy
a fourth part, only a share of the whole

explanation.definitionFit: Mercy to a defeated foe, as in 'no quarter given'; and a fourth, which is only a portion, not the entirety.

clue.text: Have misgivings about light-weight

definitions.meaning: to hesitate on grounds of conscience
an old apothecaries' unit of twenty grains, a very small weight

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hesitate from moral doubt; as a noun it is a tiny apothecaries' measure of twenty grains.

clue.text: Water — nothing more!

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, only or simply

explanation.definitionFit: A lake, chiefly in poetry and place names; also an adjective meaning simply or no more than.

clue.text: Flat that's neat

definitions.meaning: level and without bends or curves
of a drink, undiluted, without water or ice

explanation.definitionFit: Level and even without curves; and an undiluted spirit served without mixer.

clue.text: Flier getting the finest fish

parts.note: a star is the best performer
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: A bird catches the best fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A common speckled songbird is a creature that flies.

clue.text: Sped about at the church to finish off

indicators.note: the letters of 'sped' are turned about into a new order

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone raced around at church to wrap things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals a rearrangement of 'Sped'; 'at' is kept as written and the church gives its usual abbreviation. Despatch is a British spelling of dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill or deal with something quickly is to dispose of it.

clue.text: Composing thank you note for collection of pictures

parts.note: TA is an informal British way of saying thank you
TE is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Writing a thank-you letter for a gift of paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composing' seems to call for music or an anagram, but here it simply means making up the whole from two pieces. The Tate is the London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate galleries in London house the national collection of British and modern art.

clue.text: Various characters were impressed with his output

definitions.text: Various characters were impressed with his output

parts.words: Various characters were impressed with his output
parts.note: 'characters' are letters of type, and 'impressed' means pressed onto paper, not admired

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests people admired someone's work; read 'characters' as typeface letters and 'impressed' as stamped.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who presses inked type onto paper produces letters as his work.

clue.text: Forceful firm fellow

parts.note: CO is company, a business firm
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A strong, resolute man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective describing the fellow, but it is the noun, a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasive, convincing argument is a powerful one.

clue.text: City retreat where French pastry is served

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
a lair is a hideaway or den

explanation.surface: A city hideaway that serves cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London, its financial district, has EC postcodes.
explanation.definitionFit: A long choux bun filled with cream and topped with chocolate is a French cake.

clue.text: Protect key wetland in divine setting

indicators.note: the outer letters form a setting, holding the others like a jewel

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a divine or theologian
E is a musical key
a fen is marshy low-lying land

explanation.surface: Guard a vital marsh in a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is the noun, a clergyman, abbreviated DD; 'key' is the musical key, not 'important'.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard or shield something from attack is to protect it.

clue.text: Serving girls win a more workable arrangement

indicators.note: a new arrangement of these letters that works as a word, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A suggestion that waitresses could win by a better plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving girls' suggests maids, but here it means women serving in an air force; 'workable arrangement' rearranges WIN A MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who serve in the air force are female members of the armed forces.

clue.text: A quietly suffering native American

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical direction for playing quietly
an ache is a pain or suffering

explanation.surface: An indigenous American in silent pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A people of the American Southwest, known for leaders such as Geronimo.

clue.text: The singer wants a lot changed

indicators.note: the letters are changed round into a new order

explanation.surface: The vocalist needs many alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: A low female or high male voice; a person singing that part.

clue.text: The chimney-sweep's appalling ways

parts.note: grim means dreadful or appalling
E and S, east and south, are directions or ways

explanation.surface: The sweep has dreadful habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Mr Grimes is the cruel master sweep in Charles Kingsley's novel The Water-Babies.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kingsley's The Water-Babies the boy Tom works for a brutal master sweep of that name.

clue.text: A sporting event boring some folk

parts.note: flat means dull or boring
a race is a group of people of common descent

explanation.surface: A sports fixture that bores some people.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing a flat race is one run without jumps, as opposed to steeplechasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race over level ground with no hurdles is a fixture in the racing calendar.

clue.text: Item of clothing unlikely to appeal to loose women?

definitions.text: Item of clothing unlikely to appeal to loose women?

parts.words: Item of clothing unlikely to appeal to loose women?
parts.note: plays on 'loose' as the opposite of close-fitting, as well as meaning promiscuous

explanation.walkthrough: 'loose women' reads as promiscuous, but the joke is that a woman who likes loose clothes would not want this close-fitting garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting legwear garment covering the hips and legs, the opposite of loose.

clue.text: The cutting wearied and was somewhat worrying

indicators.note: THE cuts into the other word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: to have wearied someone is to have bored them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gardening cuttings that tired someone and caused mild concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cutting' looks like a garden cutting, but THE is cutting into BORED.
explanation.definitionFit: If something troubled you a little, it disturbed or perturbed you.
